extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy / classical education (readers of Plato)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive account of the education, selection, and intellectual formation of the guardian/philosopher-ruler: what studies, methods, sequence, and moral aims constitute the curriculum that turns souls from appearance to truth and prepares them to govern. Focuses on mathematical, musical, and dialectical training and the duty of rulers to descend and serve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegory of the Cave — world of sight as shadows
rubrics_metrics.description: The prison-house is the world of sight; the light of the fire is the sun; to those in the den 'the truth would be literally nothing but the shadows of the images.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains epistemic condition of ordinary humans: perceptions are shadows/appearances. The ascent out of the cave is the soul's movement toward genuine being and knowledge; initial release produces pain, bewilderment, and resistance. Anti-pattern: treating sensory shadows as full reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea of the Good appears last and must be seen with effort
rubrics_metrics.description: In the world of knowledge the idea of good appears last of all, and is seen only with an effort; when seen, it is inferred to be the universal author of all things beautiful and right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The highest object of knowledge (the Good) is not immediate; education must culminate in apprehension of the Good, which grounds reason and truth. Scoring note: attainment of the Good is the final aim of the ascent.

rubrics_metrics.name: True learning is conversion of the soul not implantation
rubrics_metrics.description: The power and capacity of learning exists in the soul already; the instrument of knowledge can only by the movement of the whole soul be turned from the world of becoming into that of being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education is turning the soul's gaze toward being (conversion), not simply putting new knowledge into an empty mind. Anti-pattern: claim that teachers can 'put knowledge into the soul' like sight into blind eyes.

rubrics_metrics.name: There must be an art of conversion (not implanting sight)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must not be wonder that there is some art which will effect conversion in the easiest and quickest manner; not implanting the faculty of sight, for that exists already, but turning it in the right direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational method should aim at reorienting innate capacities. Emphasizes method over rote delivery. Guidance: seek practices that effect re-orientation rather than mere information transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue of wisdom contains a divine element and can be perverted
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereas other virtues can be implanted by habit, the virtue of wisdom contains a divine element which always remains, and by conversion is rendered useful or, if perverted, hurtful. Example: the 'clever rogue' whose keen intelligence serves evil ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intellectual gifts must be morally directed; training must prevent cleverness being harnessed for vice. Anti-pattern: educating technical skill without moral formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best minds must be compelled to attain knowledge of the Good and then descend to rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The business of the founders of the State will be to compel the best minds to attain the greatest knowledge—they must continue to ascend until they arrive at the good; but when they have ascended we must not allow them to remain in the upper world—they must be made to descend again among the prisoners and partake of their labours and honours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and obligation: those educated to the highest knowledge are required to serve in political offices for the benefit of the whole State. Anti-pattern: allowing philosopher to remain aloof and refuse civic duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulers must be made benefactors of the State, not privileged for personal happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislator did not aim at making any one class in the State happy above the rest; happiness was to be in the whole State, and citizens are created to be instruments binding up the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justice of compelling educated rulers to govern is defended by appeal to common good. Policy criterion: rulers' duties are justified by state cohesion rather than private advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best rulers are reluctant; eagerness to rule indicates bad state
rubrics_metrics.description: The State in which the rulers are most reluctant to govern is always the best and most quietly governed, and the State in which they are most eager, the worst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attitude of rulers is an evaluative criterion: reluctance to govern (service-motivation) marks superior regimes; ambition and hunger for office predict disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must be both warriors and philosophers
rubrics_metrics.description: Our guardian is both warrior and philosopher; the new kind of knowledge must have an additional quality: usefulness in war as well as the power to draw the soul from becoming to being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum design must combine military usefulness (gymnastic, tactics) with philosophical training. Anti-pattern: training guardians only as soldiers or only as theorists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic/number: necessary study to draw soul toward being
rubrics_metrics.description: Number and calculation compel the soul towards being; arithmetic draws the soul to reason about abstract number and rebukes the introduction of visible or tangible objects into argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arithmetic must be pursued until students 'see the nature of numbers with the mind only', not for commercial ends. Anti-pattern: teaching arithmetic as mere merchant's tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry: study of the eternal (not merely practical applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The knowledge at which geometry aims is knowledge of the eternal, and not of aught perishing and transient. Geometry will draw the soul towards truth and create the spirit of philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize pure/abstract geometry and its power to raise the mind; avoid reducing geometry to 'squaring and extending' for practical aims. Anti-pattern: geometry taught only for craft/practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomy: use the heavens as pattern to apprehend true motions by reason
rubrics_metrics.description: The starry heaven should be used as a pattern and with a view to higher knowledge; true motions (absolute swiftness and slowness, true number and figure) are apprehended by reason and not by sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Astronomy should be learned by problems and in a way that leads to intelligible principles, not by slavish observation of visible particulars. Anti-pattern: taking visible heavenly particulars as eternal truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony/music: pursue for the beautiful and good, not mere sound analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pythagoreans and musicians who investigate heard harmonies but never reach problems are in error; harmony is useful if sought after with a view to the beautiful and good, otherwise useless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Music education should cultivate harmony and habituate the soul, but aim at moral and philosophical ends rather than technical taxonomy of intervals. Anti-pattern: pedantry about compressed intervals detached from moral purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studies must be interconnected; value arises when they inter-communicate
rubrics_metrics.description: When all these studies reach the point of inter-communion and connection with one another, and come to be considered in their mutual affinities, then the pursuit of them will have a value for our objects; otherwise there is no profit in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum coherence: integrate arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, harmony, gymnastic, and dialectic so they collectively direct the soul. Anti-pattern: isolated specialties without synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical study must be pursued in the spirit of the philosopher, not the shopkeeper
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic has a very great and elevating effect if pursued in the spirit of a philosopher, and not of a shopkeeper—i.e., not for buying or selling but for the sake of the soul and military/philosophical use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize orientation and intention of study: intellectual purity over commercial/practical motives. Anti-pattern: instrumental, profit-driven pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects that 'invite' intelligence present simultaneous opposites
rubrics_metrics.description: Those impressions which invite the intellect are those in which the sense intimates opposite impressions simultaneously (e.g., something seen as both hard and soft); such perplexities compel the soul to summon calculation and intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select subject-matters that problematize sense (unity vs plurality, opposites) to stimulate abstract thought. Anti-pattern: subjects fully settled by sense that do not provoke inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: use problems and dialectic as culminating method
rubrics_metrics.description: In astronomy and geometry 'we should employ problems' and avoid merely looking at visible things; the dialogue concludes that the proper culmination of the mathematical studies and the turning of the soul is dialectic—the 'hymn of dialectic.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach by posing problems that require reasoned ascent from particulars to universals; prepare students for dialectical inquiry as the highest intellectual method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct sequencing of studies matters (plane → solids → astronomy etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper order of studies matters: after plane geometry follow solids in themselves (third dimension) then astronomy; incorrect sequence (skipping solids) is an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design curriculum with logical progression from simpler to more complex/more abstract subjects. Anti-pattern: haphazard or convenience-based ordering of topics.
